title: Sedition law repeal - what replaced it under the new criminal code
p1:
The word “sedition” has disappeared from India’s new criminal laws… but does that mean the offence is gone completely?

The answer is more complicated than many people think.
p2:
A common misconception is that removing Section 124A of the Indian Penal Code ended all laws against threats to the nation’s unity. The new criminal code, Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), introduces a different provision instead.

BNS Section 152 deals with acts that threaten India’s sovereignty, unity, and integrity. The focus has shifted from the old term “sedition” to specific actions that create such threats.
p3:
The key difference is the language and approach. The law no longer uses the colonial-era label of sedition, but it still addresses serious acts that can harm national security and public order.

The practical takeaway: a change in name does not always mean a complete removal of legal consequences. The exact facts of a case still decide how the law applies.
conclusion: Do you think replacing the word “sedition” has created a meaningful legal change, or is it mainly a change in terminology?
